source_text: ΤΟΥ ΕΝ ΑΓΙΟΙΣ ΠΑΤΡΟΣ ΗΜΩΝ ΑΘΑΝΑΣΙΟΥ ΑΡΧΙΕΠΙΣΚΟΠΟΥ ΑΛΕΞΑΝΔΡΕΙΑΣ ΠΡΟΣ ΜΑΞΙΜΟΝ ΦΙΛΟΣΟΦΟΝ. Τῷ ἀγαπητῷ καὶ ἀληθῶς ποθεινοτάτῳ υἱῷ Μαξίμῳ φιλοσόφῳ, Ἀθανάσιος ἐν Κυρίῳ χαίρειν. Ἐντυχὼν τοῖς νῦν γραφεῖσι παρὰ σοῦ, τὴν μὲν σὴν εὐλάβειαν ἀπεδεξάμην, τὴν δὲ προπέτειαν τῶν μὴ νοούντων μήτε ἃ λέγουσι, μήτε περὶ τίνων διαβεβαιοῦνται, ἐπὶ πολὺ θαυμάσας, ἐβουλευσάμην ἀληθῶς σιωπῆσαι. Τὸ γὰρ ἐπὶ τοῖς οὕτω φανεροῖς καὶ πλέον φωτὸς λάμπουσιν ἀποκρίνασθαι, οὐδὲν ἕτερόν ἐστιν ἢ προφάσεις ἀναισχυντίας τοῖς οὕτω παρανομοῦσι παρέχειν. Καὶ τοῦτο παρὰ τοῦ Σωτῆρος μεμαθήκαμεν. Νιψαμένῳ γὰρ τῷ Πιλάτῳ καὶ καταλαβομένῳ τὴν συκοφαντίαν τῶν τότε Ἰουδαίων, οὐκ ἔτι ἀπεκρίνατο αὐτῷ ὁ Κύριος, ἀλλὰ μᾶλλον ἐχρημάτιζε τῇ τούτου γυναικὶ, ἵνα μὴ ἐν λόγῳ, ἀλλὰ ἐν δυνάμει πιστεύηται ὁ κρινόμενος εἶναι Θεός. Τῷ δὲ Καϊάφᾳ μὴ ἀποκρινόμενος πρὸς τὴν φλυαρίαν, αὐτὸς τῇ ἐπαγγελίᾳ τοὺς πάντας εἰς γνῶσιν μετήγαγεν. Ἐπὶ πολὺ γοῦν ὑπερτιθέμενος καὶ ὁρῶν τὴν τῶν ἀναιδευομένων λογομαχίαν, μόλις ᾐδέσθην τὸν σὸν ὑπὲρ τῆς ἀληθείας ζῆλον, καὶ ὑπηγόρευσα οὐδὲν πλέον τῶν παρὰ σοῦ γραφέντων, ἵν' οἷς ἀντείρηκεν ὁ ἐναντίος, τούτοις λοιπὸν πεισθεὶς, παύσῃ τὴν γλῶσσαν αὐτοῦ ἀπὸ κακοῦ, καὶ χείλη αὐτοῦ τοῦ μὴ λαλῆσαι δόλον. Καὶ γένοιτο μὲν τοὺς τοιούτους μηκέτι ὀνειδίσαι μετὰ τῶν παροδευόντων τότε Ἰουδαίων τὸν κρεμάμενον ἐπὶ ξύλου, Εἰ Υἱός ἐστι τοῦ Θεοῦ, σώσει αὐτόν· ἐὰν δὲ ἄρα μηδὲ οὕτως καταδύωνται, ἀλλὰ σὺ τῆς ἀποστολικῆς μνημονεύων παραγγελίας, αἱρετικὸν ἄνθρωπον μετὰ μίαν καὶ δευτέραν νουθεσίαν παραιτοῦ, εἰδὼς, ὅτι ἐξέστραπται ὁ τοιοῦτος, καὶ ἁμαρτάνει ὢν αὐτοκατάκριτος. Εἰ μὲν γὰρ Ἕλληνες ἢ τῶν Ἰουδαϊζόντων εἰσὶν οἱ τὰ τοιαῦτα τολμῶντες, ὡς μὲν Ἰουδαῖοι σκάνδαλον, ὡς δὲ Ἕλληνες μωρίαν νομιζέτωσαν τὸν σταυρὸν τοῦ Χριστοῦ· εἰ δὲ ὑποκρίνονται ὡς Χριστιανοὶ, μαθέτωσαν τὸν σταυρωθέντα Χριστὸν, Κύριον μὲν τῆς δόξης, δύναμιν δὲ Θεοῦ καὶ Θεοῦ σοφίαν αὐτὸν εἶναι. Εἰ δὲ ἀμφιβάλλουσιν, ὅτι καὶ Θεός ἐστιν, αἰδείσθωσαν τὸν Θωμᾶν τὸν ψηλαφήσαντα τὸν ἐσταυρωμένον, καὶ λέγοντα Κύριον αὐτὸν εἶναι καὶ Θεόν. Καὶ φοβείσθωσαν αὐτὸν τὸν Κύριον, τὸν μετὰ τὸ νίψαι τοὺς πόδας τῶν μαθητῶν λέγοντα· Ὑμεῖς φωνεῖτέ με ὁ Κύριος καὶ ὁ διδάσκαλος, καὶ καλῶς λέγετε· εἰμὶ γάρ. Ἐν ᾧ δὲ σώματι τυγχάνων ἔνιψε τοὺς πόδας, ἐν τούτῳ τὰς ἁμαρτίας ἡμῶν ἀνήνεγκεν ἐπὶ τὸ ξύλον. Ἐμαρτυρεῖτό τε δεσπότης τῆς κτίσεως, συστείλαντος μὲν τοῦ ἡλίου τὰς ἀκτῖνας, καὶ τῆς γῆς τρεμούσης, καὶ τῶν πετρῶν σχιζομένων, καὶ τῶν δημίων ἐπιγνόντων, ὅτι ἀληθῶς Θεοῦ Υἱός ἐστιν ὁ σταυρωθείς. Οὐ γὰρ ἀνθρώπου τινὸς ἦν τὸ βλεπόμενον σῶμα, ἀλλὰ Θεοῦ, ἐν ᾧ τυγχάνων καὶ ὅτε ἐσταυροῦτο, ἤγειρε νεκρούς. Διὸ οὐδὲ καλὸν ἐκεῖνο αὐτῶν τόλμημα τὸ λέγον, ὅτι εἰς ἄνθρωπόν τινα ἅγιον ἐγένετο ὁ τοῦ Θεοῦ Λόγος (τοῦτο γὰρ ἐν ἑκάστῳ ἐγένετο τῶν προφητῶν καὶ τῶν ἄλλων ἁγίων), ἵνα μὴ καθ' ἕκαστον γεννώμενος καὶ πάλιν ἀποθνήσκων φαίνηται. Οὐκ ἔστι δὲ οὕτως· μὴ γένοιτο! Ἀλλ' ἅπαξ ἐπὶ συντελείᾳ τῶν αἰώνων εἰς ἀθέτησιν τῆς ἁμαρτίας αὐτὸς ὁ Λόγος σὰρξ ἐγένετο, καὶ ἐκ Μαρίας τῆς Παρθένου προῆλθεν ἄνθρωπος καθ' ὁμοίωσιν ἡμετέραν, ὡς καὶ πρὸς Ἰουδαίους ἔφη· Τί ζητεῖτέ με ἀποκτεῖναι ἄνθρωπον, ὃς τὴν ἀλήθειαν ὑμῖν λελάληκα; Οὐκ ἀνθρώπου τέ τινος μετέχοντες σώματος, ἀλλὰ αὐτοῦ τοῦ Λόγου σῶμα λαμβάνοντες, θεοποιούμεθα.
thought_title: Silence before shamelessness, then the crucified Word
orientation: Athanasius opens his letter to Maximus the philosopher, explaining why he nearly kept silent before shameless opponents and then confessing the crucified Christ as God the Word made flesh.
pass_a_gloss: Of our father among the saints Athanasius, archbishop of Alexandria, to Maximus the philosopher. To the beloved and truly most longed-for son Maximus the philosopher, Athanasius in the Lord greetings. Having met with the things now written by you, I welcomed your piety, but the rashness of those who understand neither what they say nor about what things they make confident assertions, having marveled at it greatly, I resolved truly to be silent. For to answer about things so manifest and shining more than light is nothing other than to provide pretexts for shamelessness to those who so transgress the law. And this we have learned from the Savior. For when Pilate had washed and had grasped the slander of the Jews of that time, the Lord no longer answered him, but rather received a message to his wife, so that not in word but in power the one being judged might be believed to be God. And to Caiaphas, not answering his foolish talk, he himself by the promise brought all to knowledge. For a long time then I was putting it off and seeing the word-battling of those acting shamelessly, I scarcely felt shame before your zeal for the truth, and I dictated nothing more than the things written by you, so that, having been persuaded by the things which the opponent has contradicted, he may henceforth stop his tongue from evil, and his lips from speaking deceit. And may it be that such people no longer mock with the Jews passing by at that time the one hanging on a tree, 'If he is Son of God, he will save him'; but if then they do not even so sink down, but you, remembering the apostolic command, refuse a heretical man after a first and second admonition, knowing that such a one has been turned inside out and sins being self-condemned. For if Greeks or those of the Judaizers are the ones daring such things, as Jews let them consider the cross of Christ a scandal, as Greeks foolishness; but if they pretend to be Christians, let them learn that the crucified Christ is Lord of glory, power of God and wisdom of God. But if they doubt that he is also God, let them feel shame before Thomas who touched the crucified one and said that he is Lord and God. And let them fear the Lord himself, the one saying after washing the feet of the disciples: 'You call me the Lord and the teacher, and you speak well; for I am.' And in what body he was when he washed the feet, in this he bore up our sins on the tree. And he was witnessed as master of creation, the sun having drawn in its rays, and the earth trembling, and the rocks being split, and the executioners recognizing that truly Son of God is the one crucified. For the body being seen was not of some man, but of God, in which being also when he was crucified, he raised the dead. Therefore not good is that bold saying of theirs, which says that into some holy man the Word of God came (for this happened in each of the prophets and the other saints), so that he may not appear being born in each case and again dying. But it is not so; may it not be! But once at the consummation of the ages for the nullification of sin the Word himself became flesh, and from Mary the Virgin came forth man according to our likeness, as he also said to the Jews: 'Why do you seek to kill me, a man who has spoken the truth to you?' And not partaking of the body of some man, but receiving the body of the Word himself, we are made divine.

lemmas.gloss: has been turned inside out, perverted

choices.english: received a message to his wife
choices.why: χρηματίζω in the passive/active here means to receive a divine communication or warning; Pilate's wife was the recipient of the dream-warning, not the speaker
rejected: made a declaration to his wife
gave an oracle to his wife

choices.why: The perfect of ἐκστρέφω conveys a perverted, twisted state; the literal image of being turned inside out matches the strong verb and the context of a heretic's corruption
ἀθέτησις means annulment or setting aside; 'nullification' keeps the legal force of the term for sin's cancellation
The verb θεοποιέω is a strong deification term; 'made divine' is literal and preserves the passive force
ὑπαγορεύω means to dictate for another to write; Athanasius is presenting the letter as dictated, not merely composed
ἐπὶ πολύ with θαυμάζω means to marvel for a long time or greatly; 'greatly' captures the intensity of astonishment at the opponents' rashness
rejected: having wondered for a long time

pass_b_english: Having read what you have now written, I welcomed your reverence, but I marveled greatly at the rashness of those who understand neither what they say nor what they confidently assert, and I truly resolved to remain silent. For to answer things so obvious and shining more than light is nothing other than to provide excuses for shamelessness to those who break the law in this way. And this we have learned from the Savior. For when Pilate had washed his hands and grasped the slander of the Jews of that time, the Lord no longer answered him, but rather sent a divine warning to his wife, so that the one being judged might be believed to be God, not in word but in power. And by not answering Caiaphas in his foolish talk, he himself by his promise brought all to knowledge. So after long delay and seeing the word-battling of those who act shamelessly, I at last gave way out of respect for your zeal for the truth, and I dictated nothing more than what you wrote, so that you, by the very things the opponent has contradicted, may finally stop his tongue from evil and his lips from speaking deceit (Psalm 33:13-14 LXX; 34:12-13 Hebrew). And may such people no longer taunt, with the Jews who passed by then, the one hanging on the tree, saying, “If he is the Son of God, he will save himself” (Matthew 27:40). But if they do not sink down even so, then you, remembering the apostolic command, reject a heretical man after a first and second warning, knowing that such a person is warped and sins, being self-condemned (Titus 3:10-11). For if those who dare such things are Greeks or Judaizers, let them as Jews consider the cross of Christ a scandal, and as Greeks foolishness (1 Corinthians 1:23); but if they pretend to be Christians, let them learn that the crucified Christ is Lord of glory, the power of God and the wisdom of God (1 Corinthians 1:24). And if they doubt that he is also God, let them reverence Thomas, who touched the crucified one and said that he is Lord and God. And let them fear the Lord himself, the one saying after washing the disciples’ feet, “You call me the Lord and the teacher, and you speak well, for I am” (John 13:13). And in the body in which he was present when he washed their feet, in that same body he bore our sins upon the tree. And he was witnessed as master of creation, when the sun drew in its rays, and the earth trembled, and the rocks were split, and the executioners recognized that truly the crucified one is the Son of God. For the body that was seen was not some man’s, but God’s, in which he was present even when he was crucified, and he raised the dead. Therefore their bold saying is not good, which says that the Word of God came into some holy man—for this happened in each of the prophets and the other saints—so that he might not appear to be born and dying again in each one. But it is not so; may it never be! But once, at the consummation of the ages, for the nullification of sin, the Word himself became flesh, and from Mary the Virgin he came forth as man in our likeness, as he also said to the Jews, “Why do you seek to kill me, a man who has spoken the truth to you?” (John 8:40). And it is not by partaking of some man’s body, but by receiving the body of the Word himself, that we are made divine.

problems.quote: I scarcely respected your zeal for the truth
problems.source_quote: μόλις ᾐδέσθην τὸν σὸν ὑπὲρ τῆς ἀληθείας ζῆλον
problems.why: ᾐδέσθην means 'I was ashamed to disregard' or 'I had regard for', not 'scarcely respected'.
problems.fix: I could scarcely disregard your zeal for the truth

problems.quote: the one being judged is God not in word but in power
problems.source_quote: ἵνα μὴ ἐν λόγῳ, ἀλλὰ ἐν δυνάμει πιστεύηται ὁ κρινόμενος εἶναι Θεός
problems.why: Missing 'to be believed/trusted'; the point is that Christ is believed to be God by power, not merely asserted by word.
problems.fix: so that the one being judged might be believed to be God, not in word but in power
problems.ruling: πιστεύηται = 'may be believed/trusted'; English omits this, making 'is God' a statement rather than something to be believed.

problems.fix: you may stop his tongue from evil
problems.ruling: παύσῃ is 3rd sg. aorist subjunctive ('may he stop'), not 2nd person. 'His tongue' confirms 3rd person reference to the opponent.

problems.ruling: LXX numbering is Ps 33:14, not 34:13. Wrong reference if LXX numbering required.

μόλις ᾐδέσθην means 'I scarcely respected/honored', not 'disregarded'; fixed to 'I could scarcely resist honoring'.

fixed.quote: but rather spoke to his wife
fixed.fix: but rather sent a divine warning to his wife
fixed.note: Active ἐχρημάτιζε means 'gave an oracle or warning' (the wife's dream in Matthew 27:19), which the 'in power, not in word' point depends on. The proposed fix gets the agency wrong.

fixed.quote: I could scarcely resist honoring your zeal
fixed.fix: I at last gave way out of respect for your zeal
fixed.note: μόλις ᾐδέσθην means he gave way only reluctantly, out of respect; 'could scarcely resist' suggests eagerness and clashes with 'after long delay'. The proposed fix reverses the sense.

fixed.quote: If he is the Son of God, let him save himself
fixed.fix: If he is the Son of God, he will save himself
fixed.note: σώσει is future indicative, not an imperative; read as αὑτόν it means 'himself', and the proposed 'he will save him' leaves unclear who saves whom.
ἐξέστραπται in Titus 3:11 means perverted or warped; 'turned inside out' is an etymological calque that misleads the reader, and the proposed fix offers slash-separated options rather than one text.

dismissed.quote: And may such people no longer taunt, with the Jews who passed by then, the one hanging on the tree
dismissed.why: γένοιτο + accusative + infinitive is optative of wish: 'May it come about that such people no longer taunt...' English loses the wish construction.
dismissed.note: 'May such people no longer taunt' already expresses the γένοιτο wish in natural English.

dismissed.quote: And he was witnessed as master of creation
dismissed.why: Ἐμαρτυρεῖτο is passive, 'he was witnessed/borne witness to', but δεσπότης is nominative predicate: 'and he was witnessed to as master of creation' or 'and he, the master of creation, was witnessed to'.
dismissed.note: 'He was witnessed as master of creation' already renders the passive verb with δεσπότης as its predicate.
